classification.difficultyReason: Determine an algebraic unknown, then justify both pairs of parallel sides using the converse of the co-interior angle property.

content.prompt: Show that this shape is a parallelogram. Justify your answer clearly.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 13 figure beneath the prompt, on the left.
spec.description: Unshaded slanted quadrilateral, with approximately horizontal top and bottom edges and four labelled interior-angle arcs. No printed vertex names, parallel markers or equality ticks.
spec.mathematics: Top-left angle (3x−5)°, top-right (4x+10)°, bottom-left (5x−15)°, bottom-right (2x+20)°. Coordinates reproduce the source appearance without establishing parallelism as a given.
spec.answerVisibility: All four algebraic angle labels are permanent givens; no solved values or proof marks appear.

answer.short: $x=25$. The angles are $70^\circ$, $110^\circ$, $70^\circ$ and $110^\circ$ in clockwise order from the top-left. Adjacent angles sum to $180^\circ$, proving both pairs of opposite sides parallel by the converse of the co-interior angle property. Hence the shape is a parallelogram.
answer.worked:
The interior angles of a quadrilateral sum to $360^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}
(3x-5)+(4x+10)+(5x-15)+(2x+20)&=360\\
14x+10&=360\\
14x&=350\\
x&=25
\end{align*}$$
Substituting $x=25$ gives the top-left, top-right, bottom-left and bottom-right angles as $70^\circ$, $110^\circ$, $110^\circ$ and $70^\circ$, respectively.
$$\begin{align*}
(5x-15)+(2x+20)&=180\\
(3x-5)+(4x+10)&=180\\
(3x-5)+(5x-15)&=180\\
(4x+10)+(2x+20)&=180
\end{align*}$$
The first two sums show that the left and right sides are parallel. The last two show that the top and bottom sides are parallel. In each case, co-interior angles sum to $180^\circ$, so the lines are parallel by the converse of the co-interior angle property. Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel; therefore the quadrilateral is a parallelogram.
